clues: the bottom of the case bulges outward
the touchpad is pushed up and hard to click
the laptop rocks when it sits on a flat desk
the bulging laptop is left on the charger day and night

answer.cause: a swollen lithium-ion battery
answer.action: Stop using the laptop and have the battery removed and recycled safely

appliesWhen: the case bulges because the battery inside has swollen
explanation: Age, overcharging, or a defect can make a lithium-ion battery swell and push the case and touchpad out of shape. A swollen battery must not be punctured; remove it with care, keep it cool and dark, and recycle it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

clues: the laptop runs only about 20 minutes when unplugged
the laptop works normally on AC power but dies soon after it is unplugged
the laptop that runs only minutes on battery is five years old
the charge level drops fast and then the laptop shuts off

answer.cause: a worn-out battery that no longer holds a charge
answer.action: Replace the battery with a new one made for this laptop model

appliesWhen: the laptop runs well on AC power but the battery runs down very quickly
explanation: A battery can be recharged only a limited number of cycles. After a few years it loses charge quickly, and a very short runtime means it must be replaced.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

clues: the laptop has charged only now and then since it fell while it was plugged in
the charge light comes on only when the plug is held at an angle
the power port wiggles and charging stops when the cord moves
a known good adapter of the right model does not charge it either

answer.cause: a damaged DC jack
answer.action: Have the DC jack on the motherboard repaired or replaced

appliesWhen: the power port is loose or damaged and the laptop charges only now and then
explanation: The DC jack is soldered to the motherboard and is easily damaged when a laptop falls on its plug. A jack that charges only at an angle is loose or broken and must be repaired.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

clues: the laptop will not charge on a charger borrowed from a coworker
the borrowed plug fits, but the battery charge never rises
the charger that fails came with a different model of the same brand
the laptop's own charger, left at home today, always charged it normally

answer.cause: an AC adapter from a different laptop model
answer.action: Use the AC adapter made for this laptop model

firstStep: Compare the adapter's output rating with the rating on the laptop
appliesWhen: the laptop is plugged into a charger that belongs to another model
explanation: Laptop AC adapters are fixed-input supplies made for one model. An adapter from another model, even one only a volt or two different, usually will not power or charge the laptop.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

clues: one key has to be pressed very hard to type
one key stays down after it is pressed while the others work normally
the key problem began after coffee was spilled near the laptop yesterday
a dried brown residue shows around the edges of the hard-to-press key

answer.cause: a sticky key switch from a spilled drink
answer.action: Remove the keycap and clean the key switch underneath

appliesWhen: one or two keys stick after a spill but the rest of the keyboard works
explanation: A spill or heavy use can make a key switch stick. Removing the keycap and cleaning the switch usually fixes it; if not, the keyboard must be replaced.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

clues: no key on the built-in keyboard works
the laptop whose keyboard is dead is carried between sites every day
the keyboard stopped working after the laptop was jostled in a bag
even the Fn and Caps Lock keys do nothing

answer.cause: a loose keyboard ribbon cable
answer.action: Lift the keyboard and reseat its ribbon cable on the motherboard

appliesWhen: the whole built-in keyboard stops working after the laptop is moved or jostled
explanation: The keyboard connects to the motherboard with a ribbon cable that can work loose when a laptop is moved around. When every key fails at once, lift the keyboard and attach the cable firmly.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

clues: the letters U, I, and O type 4, 5, and 6
the wrong characters began when the user came back from using an external keyboard at a desk
a password that worked yesterday is now rejected
a small light near the top of the keyboard is on while the wrong characters appear

answer.cause: the numeric keypad turned on by Num Lock
answer.action: Press the Num Lock key to turn off the numeric keypad

firstStep: Check whether the keypad indicator light is on
appliesWhen: some letter keys type numbers because the embedded numeric keypad is on
explanation: On small laptop keyboards the numeric keypad shares keys with letters. When Num Lock is on, those letters type numbers, and one press of Num Lock turns it off.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

clues: several keys stopped working after a heavy box was dropped on the open laptop
several keycaps are missing or tilted
the keyboard surface is no longer flat

answer.cause: a bent keyboard from a heavy impact
answer.action: Replace the whole keyboard

appliesWhen: the keyboard is bent or warped from a heavy blow
explanation: A heavy object or a heavy hand can bend or warp a laptop keyboard. That damage usually cannot be repaired, so the keyboard is replaced.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

clues: a second memory module was installed this morning, but the memory total did not change
the System Information tool lists only one memory module after the upgrade
the laptop boots and runs normally apart from the missing memory
the access cover would not close flat after the new module went in

answer.cause: a new memory module that is not fully seated
answer.action: Power off the laptop and press the new module into its slot until the clips lock

appliesWhen: new memory was just added and the system does not count it
explanation: Upgraded memory that the BIOS/UEFI does not see is usually not installed properly. Turn the laptop off, reseat the SODIMM until it clicks into place, and reboot.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

clues: the laptop gives a series of continuous beeps at power on
the screen stays black at power on
the laptop, used on a dusty shop floor, has started beeping at startup
no memory has been changed since the startup beeps began

answer.cause: dirty contacts on the memory modules
answer.action: Clean the memory contacts with compressed air or a RAM cleaner

appliesWhen: the laptop beeps and will not boot after being used in a dusty place
explanation: Continuous beeps at startup point to memory, and laptops in harsh places often get dirty memory contacts. Clean the contacts, reseat the modules, and swap in known good RAM if the beeps continue.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

clues: the laptop makes clicking and grinding sounds
files take a long time to open and some are corrupt
the noises began after the laptop was dropped while it was running

answer.cause: a failing magnetic hard drive
answer.action: Replace the drive with an SSD and restore the user's data

firstStep: Back up the user's data before the drive fails completely
appliesWhen: a spinning drive makes noise and files open slowly or are corrupt
explanation: Laptop drives take many bumps and will fail in time, and a magnetic drive that clicks after a drop is failing. Replace it, ideally with a faster, shock-resistant SSD.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware

clues: the wireless light above the keyboard is off and no networks show
the connection stopped right after the user pressed several function keys
the wireless adapter shows as enabled in Device Manager but cannot connect
the laptop was on Wi-Fi an hour ago but now lists no networks

answer.cause: the wireless adapter switched off with the Wi-Fi function key
answer.action: Press the Wi-Fi function key or button to turn the adapter back on

appliesWhen: the laptop's wireless button or function key has turned the adapter off
explanation: Many laptops have a Wi-Fi button or function key that turns the built-in adapter on and off. When it is off, the laptop cannot connect even though the adapter is enabled in the OS.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

clues: the laptop has no Wi-Fi and its wireless adapter is missing from Device Manager
reinstalling the wireless driver did not help
a USB Wi-Fi adapter connects normally while the built-in wireless does not
pressing the Wi-Fi key does not bring the wireless back

answer.cause: a failed internal wireless card
answer.action: Replace the wireless card with a compatible M.2 card

appliesWhen: the internal wireless card is no longer detected at all
explanation: When the OS cannot see the internal adapter at all but a USB adapter works, the internal card has failed. Laptop wireless cards, usually M.2 or Mini PCIe, can be replaced.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware

clues: the Wi-Fi has been weak since the display panel was replaced last week
the weak signal began after the wireless card was taken out during the display repair
the signal is weak even next to the access point
other laptops get a strong signal in the same spot where this one is weak

answer.cause: an antenna wire left disconnected from the wireless card
answer.action: Reconnect the antenna wires to the main and auxiliary posts on the wireless card

appliesWhen: an antenna wire was not reconnected to the wireless card after a repair
explanation: The Wi-Fi antenna runs through the display, so display repairs mean taking the antenna leads off the wireless card. If a lead is not reconnected, the card still works but the signal is very weak.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware

clues: the Wi-Fi has been unreliable since the display hinge cracked in a fall
the connection drops when the lid is tilted
the signal changes as the loose hinge moves

answer.cause: antenna wiring damaged inside a broken hinge
answer.action: Replace the hinge and the damaged antenna wiring

appliesWhen: the Wi-Fi drops as the lid moves after the hinge was damaged
explanation: The Wi-Fi antenna wiring runs up through a hinge into the display. A damaged hinge can pinch or break those wires, so the signal changes as the lid moves.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware

clues: the camera's activity light turns on, but the video window stays black
the Device Manager list shows the camera working with no errors, yet calls show no picture
the black video window brightens a little when the lid is pointed at a bright lamp
a driver reinstall did not bring back the picture in any video app

answer.cause: tape or a privacy cover over the webcam lens
answer.action: Remove the cover from the webcam lens

appliesWhen: the camera runs but something blocks its lens
explanation: A camera that turns on its light but shows only black is working; something is in front of the lens. Many users cover webcams with tape or a cover for privacy.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

clues: no app can find a camera
the camera stopped working right after the user changed privacy settings
the camera stopped working even though the laptop has not been dropped or opened
the camera is still listed in Device Manager but apps cannot use it

answer.cause: the webcam turned off in the OS or with a function key
answer.action: Turn the webcam back on in the OS settings or with its function key

firstStep: Check the camera's privacy settings and its function key
appliesWhen: the camera is present but has been turned off in software or with a key
explanation: A laptop camera can be turned off with a function key or in the operating system. Check those options before replacing a webcam.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

clues: the camera is missing from Device Manager even after a driver update
the built-in camera stopped working after the display took a hard knock
a USB webcam works with the same apps while the built-in camera does not
the camera is turned on in the OS settings but no app finds it

answer.cause: a failed webcam module
answer.action: Replace the webcam module in the display with an identical part

appliesWhen: the built-in camera is no longer detected after damage
explanation: When the built-in camera is not detected even with current drivers and its settings turned on, the module has failed. It sits above the screen behind the bezel and is replaced with an identical part.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

clues: others in the meeting cannot hear the user
a small light has glowed on one function key since the microphone went silent
the meeting app still lists the built-in microphone but shows no input
the microphone went silent after the user pressed keys at the top of the keyboard

answer.cause: the microphone muted with its hardware key
answer.action: Press the microphone key to unmute the microphone

appliesWhen: the microphone has been silenced with its key on the keyboard
explanation: Many laptops have a function key that mutes the microphone and lights up while it is on. The microphone is still listed but sends no sound until the key is pressed again.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

clues: the meeting app shows no microphone to choose from
the microphone stopped working after an administrator tightened privacy settings
no function key light is on, yet no app can use the microphone

answer.cause: the microphone disabled in the operating system
answer.action: Enable the microphone on the Recording tab of the Sound settings

appliesWhen: the microphone has been turned off in the operating system
explanation: A microphone can be disabled in the operating system, for example on the Recording tab of the Sound dialog box in Windows. Apps then cannot see it until it is enabled again.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

clues: others say the user sounds muffled and far away
the muffled sound began after the user put tape over the camera and the small holes beside it
the input level meter moves but stays low

answer.cause: tape over the microphone openings
answer.action: Remove the tape from the microphone openings

appliesWhen: something covers the microphone openings and muffles the sound
explanation: The microphone often sits next to the webcam lens. Tape over its openings muffles the sound but does not stop it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

need: add a second sign-in factor to the sales laptops
clues: the users want to sign in with a touch instead of typing a code
the laptops have no built-in way to scan a body feature
each laptop has a free USB port
appliesWhen: users must sign in with a body feature as well as a password
explanation: Biometrics identify a person by a physical feature such as a fingerprint. A USB fingerprint reader adds that factor to a laptop that has no built-in sensor, which makes sign-in multifactor.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware

need: keep laptops at a public counter from being carried off
clues: visitors must still be able to use the laptops
staff often step away from the table
the table has a sturdy metal leg
appliesWhen: the main risk is someone walking off with the device
explanation: A cable lock anchors a laptop to a solid structure, much like a bicycle lock. It is the best way to deter theft of the device itself.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware

need: stop people nearby from reading a laptop screen
clues: the user works on payroll data on trains
strangers often sit beside the user
the screen must stay easy to read from straight in front
appliesWhen: others nearby must not be able to read the display
explanation: A privacy screen narrows the viewing angle so only the person directly in front can read the display. It stops shoulder surfing in public places.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware

need: close a short-range way that a nearby attacker could read data from the laptops
clues: the laptops are never used to tap and pay
the Wi-Fi and Bluetooth radios must stay available
security staff worry about a scanner held a few centimeters away

answer.item: Turn off NFC in the operating system

appliesWhen: a laptop's near-field radio is a risk and is not needed
explanation: NFC is a two-way, short-range radio that an attacker with a scanner could try to use. If it is not needed, turn it off on its own in the OS, which leaves the other radios on.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

need: make an older laptop start and open files much faster
clues: the current drive has spinning platters
the laptop takes several minutes to start
the laptop is bumped often in the field
the laptop runs hot
appliesWhen: storage must be faster, cooler, and more shock resistant than a spinning drive
explanation: An SSD has no moving parts, so it is much faster than a magnetic drive, makes less heat, and handles bumps better. Replacing the drive is a common way to speed up an older laptop.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware

need: add memory to a laptop so more apps can run at once
clues: the installed memory module has 262 pins
the laptop slows down with many browser tabs open
an empty memory slot sits under the access cover
the memory is not soldered to the motherboard
appliesWhen: the laptop needs more memory and has a free memory slot
explanation: Laptops use small outline DIMMs, and a 262-pin module is DDR5 (DDR4 has 260 pins). Versions are not interchangeable, so the new module must match the laptop's slot.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware

need: give a laptop faster Wi-Fi and Bluetooth from inside the case
clues: the current wireless card supports only 802.11n
the card sits in a 2230 slot held by one screw
the main and auxiliary antenna leads are already in the case
the user also needs newer Bluetooth

answer.item: An M.2 Wi-Fi and Bluetooth combo card

appliesWhen: the laptop needs newer internal Wi-Fi and Bluetooth and has a slot for it
explanation: Laptop wireless cards can be upgraded, and combination Wi-Fi and Bluetooth cards often use the M.2 2230 form factor. The existing antenna leads connect to the new card.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware

need: give a laptop newer Wi-Fi when its wireless cannot be upgraded inside
clues: the wireless chip is soldered to the motherboard
the laptop has a free USB 3.0 port on each side
the adapter can be moved to the side that faces the access point
appliesWhen: the laptop has no internal slot for a new wireless card
explanation: When there is no M.2 slot for wireless, an external USB Wi-Fi adapter adds the connection. Placing it in the USB port that faces the access point can improve the signal.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

need: let users unplug the camera completely when they are not in a meeting
clues: the security team worries that malware could turn on a camera without anyone knowing
the built-in cameras will be removed
users also want better video quality
appliesWhen: users must be able to physically disconnect the camera
explanation: Some companies remove built-in webcams and use external USB webcams instead. Users can unplug them when not in use, and they often give better video.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

clues: the phone has no cellular signal, Wi-Fi, or Bluetooth
the phone has had no connections since the user got off a flight this morning
contactless payments fail too
the user cannot make calls or browse the web

answer.cause: airplane mode left turned on
answer.action: Turn off airplane mode in the quick settings or Control Center

firstStep: Check the notification bar for the airplane icon
appliesWhen: every radio on the device is off at once, including cellular
explanation: Airplane mode turns off the cellular radio and usually Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and NFC as well. Users often forget to turn it off after a flight.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 1: Monitoring, Maintaining, and Replacing Mobile Device Hardware

clues: the phone will not stay on the office Wi-Fi
the phone that will not join the office Wi-Fi appears as a Wi-Fi network on nearby laptops
the phone has used only cellular data since the user shared its connection on a trip last week

answer.cause: the mobile hotspot left on, which turns off the phone's Wi-Fi
answer.action: Turn off the hotspot and reconnect the phone to the office Wi-Fi

appliesWhen: the phone is still sharing its cellular connection with other devices
explanation: When a phone's mobile hotspot is on, its own Wi-Fi is turned off, so it can use only cellular data. Turning the hotspot off lets it join Wi-Fi again.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 10: Mobile Connectivity and Application Support

clues: the phone sees the office network but fails to join it
the phone fails to join after the user typed the long passcode on the onscreen keyboard
other phones join the same network without trouble while this one fails

answer.cause: a mistyped Wi-Fi passcode
answer.action: Forget the network and enter the passcode again with care

appliesWhen: the device sees the network but is refused when it joins
explanation: A device joins Wi-Fi only when the passcode is right; then it gets an IP address. Long passcodes typed on an onscreen keyboard are easy to get wrong.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support

clues: the map app cannot show where the user is
other apps work online normally, but the map cannot find the user
the map has not shown the position since the user turned off several privacy settings last week

answer.cause: location services turned off on the device
answer.action: Turn on location services and allow the map app to use them

appliesWhen: apps cannot get the device's position because location is off
explanation: GPS and other location-based apps cannot work when location services are off. The setting is turned on in the device's settings, and each app can be allowed separately.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 10: Mobile Connectivity and Application Support

clues: the new phone cannot find the headset that worked with the user's old phone
the headset that the new phone cannot find is still paired with an old phone that is on in the user's bag
the headset plays its connected tone but no sound comes from the new phone

answer.cause: the headset still connected to the old phone
answer.action: Disconnect or forget the headset on the old phone, then pair it with the new one

appliesWhen: the accessory is still connected to a different phone
explanation: A Bluetooth accessory connects to only one mobile device at a time. Unpair or forget it on the old device before pairing it with the new one.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support

clues: the new speaker never shows in the phone's list of devices
the phone has Bluetooth on and is scanning, but finds nothing
the speaker that the phone cannot find shows a solid light instead of a flashing one

answer.cause: a speaker that is not in pairing mode
answer.action: Press and hold the speaker's Bluetooth button until its light flashes, then scan again

appliesWhen: the accessory was never put into its discovery mode
explanation: A Bluetooth accessory must be put into pairing (discovery) mode, often by holding its button until a light flashes. Only then does it show in the phone's list of devices.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 10: Mobile Connectivity and Application Support

clues: the phone lists the car kit in its scan results, but pairing fails
pairing fails right after the car kit asks for a code
pairing failed after the user guessed 1234 at the code prompt

answer.cause: the wrong PIN code entered during pairing
answer.action: Pair again and enter the PIN from the device's documentation, such as 0000

appliesWhen: pairing fails at the step that asks for a code
explanation: Some Bluetooth devices need a PIN code to pair, and many use a default such as 0000. A wrong code makes the pairing fail even though the device is found.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support

clues: the user reached the monthly data limit in the second week
the user who hit the data limit early records many videos each day
the backup app is the top data user in the phone's settings this month

answer.cause: a photo and video backup running over cellular data
answer.action: Set the backup app to sync over Wi-Fi only

appliesWhen: large backups use the cellular plan instead of Wi-Fi
explanation: Syncing over a cellular connection counts against the plan's data cap. Large photo and video backups should run on Wi-Fi or at off-peak times.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 10: Mobile Connectivity and Application Support

clues: the phone stopped getting mail the day after the user changed the email password on the PC
mail on the PC still works, but the phone stopped getting mail
the phone's mail app keeps asking the user to sign in

answer.cause: an old email password still saved on the phone
answer.action: Update the saved password in the phone's mail account settings

appliesWhen: the account password changed but the phone still uses the old one
explanation: A mobile mail app keeps the password it was set up with. After a password change elsewhere, the phone fails to sign in until the saved password is updated.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support

clues: new email arrives on the phone, but new contacts do not
contacts added on the PC never appear on the phone
calendar events show up on both devices, unlike the new contacts

answer.cause: contact sync turned off for the mail account
answer.action: Turn on contact sync for the account in the phone's settings

appliesWhen: mail syncs but one data type, such as contacts, does not
explanation: Email, calendars, and contacts usually sync together through the mail account, but each can be turned on or off on its own. When only contacts are missing, their sync setting is off.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 10: Mobile Connectivity and Application Support

clues: the company mail app shows a message about a device policy
the company apps stopped working the day after the user removed the screen lock
the phone is enrolled like the others, but only this one is blocked

answer.cause: a phone that no longer meets the MDM security policy
answer.action: Set a screen lock that meets the policy so the MDM marks the phone compliant

appliesWhen: a managed device breaks a company policy and is blocked
explanation: MDM software checks enrolled devices against company policy. A device out of compliance can be locked out of company resources until the problem, such as a missing screen lock, is fixed.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 10: Mobile Connectivity and Application Support

need: get several devices online at a site with no network
clues: the devices have Wi-Fi but no cellular radio
the devices are spread across different rooms
no cable can reach all the devices
appliesWhen: several Wi-Fi devices must share a phone's cellular connection at once
explanation: A mobile hotspot shares the phone's cellular Internet connection with other Wi-Fi devices. It can serve several devices at once, though speed, data cost, and security are trade-offs.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 10: Mobile Connectivity and Application Support

need: get one laptop online at a site with no network
clues: the laptop's Wi-Fi adapter has failed
a USB cable for the phone is at hand
the phone should charge while it shares data
appliesWhen: one device must share the phone's cellular data over a cable
explanation: Tethering shares the phone's cellular connection with one device, often over a USB cable. It works without Wi-Fi on the laptop and keeps the phone charging.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 10: Mobile Connectivity and Application Support

need: add a local carrier line to a phone for a trip abroad
clues: the phone has no card tray
the new line must be set up remotely by the carrier
the home line must stay active on the same phone
appliesWhen: a carrier line must be added remotely without a physical card
explanation: An eSIM is built into the phone and is set up remotely by the carrier, so no card is swapped. It can hold more than one line at the same time.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 10: Mobile Connectivity and Application Support

need: use a local carrier for cheaper data during a trip abroad
clues: the phone has a small card tray on its side
the phone is an older model that cannot get a carrier profile over the air
the user will keep the home card safe to put back after the trip

answer.item: A physical SIM card from a local carrier

appliesWhen: the phone takes a removable card and has no embedded option
explanation: A SIM card holds the account and carrier data that a phone needs to join a cellular network. On a phone with a card tray, a traveler can swap in a local carrier's card and put the original back later.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support

need: stop all of a phone's radios from sending with one control
clues: the user will switch everything back on as soon as the visit ends
the phone must stay powered on to show saved files
the user is entering an area that bans transmitting devices
appliesWhen: every wireless radio must be turned off while the device stays on
explanation: Airplane mode turns off the device's wireless radios, including cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth, while the device keeps running. Every device must have it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 10: Mobile Connectivity and Application Support

need: make hands-free calls in an older car
clues: the car has no CarPlay or Android Auto support
the car stereo has a wireless phone option
calls must play through the car speakers

answer.item: Bluetooth pairing with the car's audio system

appliesWhen: a phone must link to a nearby accessory without a cable
explanation: When a car does not support CarPlay or Android Auto, it may still support Bluetooth. Pairing the phone with the car allows hands-free calls and texts.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support

need: control the settings and security on all company-owned phones
clues: the company bought and owns every phone
a lost phone must be locked or wiped as a whole
settings and updates must be pushed from one console
appliesWhen: the company must manage and secure whole devices from one console
explanation: MDM software enrolls devices and lets admins configure, update, track, lock, and wipe them from one console. It fits corporate-owned devices, where the whole device belongs to the company.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 10: Mobile Connectivity and Application Support

need: protect company data on phones that employees own
clues: the phones belong to the employees
a remote wipe must leave personal photos alone
only the corporate apps and their data must be controlled

answer.item: Mobile application management (MAM) for the corporate apps

appliesWhen: only the corporate apps and data on a personal device must be managed
explanation: Under a BYOD plan, wiping a whole lost phone would erase the user's own files. MAM installs, controls, and wipes only the corporate apps and their data.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 10: Mobile Connectivity and Application Support; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support

need: track delivery vans precisely on rural roads
clues: the vans often drive where there is no cell coverage
positions must be accurate to about 10 meters
the company does not want to pay a carrier for location
appliesWhen: an accurate position is needed outdoors, even without cell reception
explanation: GPS uses satellites, is free to use, and is accurate to about 10 meters outdoors. Cellular location needs cell reception, is less precise, and is sold by carriers.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 10: Mobile Connectivity and Application Support; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support

need: find the rough position of older company phones in the city
clues: the old phones have no satellite receiver
a position within a few hundred meters is good enough
the phones always have strong signal from several towers
appliesWhen: a rough position is enough and the device has good cell reception
explanation: Cellular location estimates a phone's position from its signal to one or more cell towers. It is less precise than GPS but needs no satellite receiver, and more towers make it more accurate.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 10: Mobile Connectivity and Application Support; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support

need: lock company tablets automatically when they are taken off the site
clues: the property has a clearly mapped boundary
the tablets already report their location
staff often forget to leave the tablets behind
appliesWhen: an action must start when a device enters or leaves a set area
explanation: Geofencing draws a virtual boundary around a real place using location data. When a device enters or leaves that area, an action such as a lock is triggered.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support

need: let a delivery app use the phone's position without tracking the user all day
clues: the user does not want to be tracked when the app is closed
the app needs the position during deliveries
other apps must keep their own settings

answer.item: The app's "While using the app" location permission

appliesWhen: one app needs location only while it is open
explanation: iOS and Android let each app have its own location permission, such as Never, While Using the App, or Always. While using the app gives location only when the app is open.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 10: Mobile Connectivity and Application Support

need: keep files, contacts, and calendars the same on a phone, a tablet, and a home PC
clues: the user works from many places
the devices are rarely near each other
the data must still be there if the phone is lost
appliesWhen: data must match across several devices in different places
explanation: Syncing to the cloud keeps the same data on every device over the Internet, and it is the most common option. The data stays safe on the service if a device is lost.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 10: Mobile Connectivity and Application Support

need: copy photos and files from a phone to the office PC without the Internet
clues: company policy blocks cloud storage
the phone and the PC sit on the same desk
a USB cable is at hand

answer.item: A USB connection to the PC set to file transfer

appliesWhen: data must move to a nearby computer without an Internet service
explanation: A phone connected to a Windows PC by USB shows up in File Explorer once its USB option is set to file transfer. No cloud service or data plan is used.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support

need: sync company email, contacts, and calendars to staff phones
clues: the company runs Microsoft Exchange Server
staff use both iOS and Android phones
meetings must appear on the phones automatically
appliesWhen: mail, contacts, and calendars must sync with a Microsoft Exchange server
explanation: Exchange ActiveSync syncs email, contacts, and calendars between many kinds of devices and Microsoft Exchange Server.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 3: Mobile Device Network Connectivity and Application Support

need: keep photo backups from using up a small cellular data plan
clues: the user takes hundreds of photos each week
the user has Wi-Fi at home and at the office
the backups can wait a few hours

answer.item: Set the backup app to sync over Wi-Fi only

appliesWhen: syncing must not count against a cellular data cap
explanation: Syncing over cellular counts against a plan's data cap. Letting large backups wait for Wi-Fi, or run at off-peak hours, keeps the plan's data for other uses.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 10: Mobile Connectivity and Application Support

task: connecting a new Bluetooth headset to a user's phone

steps.do: Put the headset into pairing mode
steps.done: put the headset into pairing mode

steps.do: Scan for the headset on the phone and select it
steps.done: found the headset on the phone and selected it

steps.do: Enter the PIN code if the headset asks for one
Test the connection with a call or audio
steps.done: tested the connection with a call

explanation: CompTIA's Bluetooth setup order is to enable Bluetooth, enable pairing, find the device, enter the PIN code, and test connectivity.
